title: Attention tile adapter for quantized streaming decode
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Quantized inference (INT8/FP8) yields large throughput gains but introduces variable dequantization overhead at attention boundaries and during decode/prefill transitions. On streaming workloads the decode path switches between prefill and incremental decode frequently; current kernel selection heuristics often choose mismatched kernels that cause extra copies, per-token dequant ops, and KV layout conversions, which increase p50/p95 latency and CPU overhead.

Goal: Implement an attention-tile adapter layer and selection heuristics that: (1) route batches to quant-friendly attention kernels when the KV format and sequence lengths align, (2) avoid per-token dequantization by deferring mixed-precision handoff to tile boundaries, and (3) provide a low-cost, fallback-aware score for runtime selection so streaming decode paths benefit without regressions for edge cases.

Scope: prototype runtime adapter + benchmark harness + opt-in feature flag. Integration points: kernel selector, KV cache layout manager, routing policy, Console metrics for new signals (tile-match-rate, deferred-dequant-count).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Adapter routes >= 80% of steady-state streaming tokens to quant-friendly attention kernels for benchmarked RAG-like workload; 2) End-to-end p95 latency for 8-token incremental decode decreases by >=10% vs current mainline on A100/RTX-class; 3) No increase in failure rate: numeric regressions within eval thresholds (per-prompt similarity >= 0.995) or automatic fallback to fp16; 4) Feature gate available with observability (tile-match-rate, dequant-savings) and can be toggled per-customer.
implementation_notes:
Design: tile the attention kv space into fixed-size chunks (tile_size=128 by default) and annotate KV buffers with tile alignment metadata. The adapter inspects incoming request characteristics (seq_len, cached_tiles, quant_format) and computes a lightweight composite score: tile_match_score * quant_compat_score - conversion_cost_estimate. If score >= threshold then route to INT8/FP8 fastpath kernel that assumes sticky quant layout; otherwise choose mixed-precision fp16 kernel.

Optimizations: (a) defer dequant to tile boundaries by accumulating microbatches until tile-complete; (b) zero-copy tile handoff using pinned device memory for cross-kernel stages; (c) amortize scale/unscale operations across the tile instead of per-head; (d) use a compact metadata header per cache shard to avoid per-token CPU work.

Fallbacks: if numeric quality falls below eval thresholds or if model layer contains unsupported ops, automatically fall back with a per-request debug tag so Console can surface incident.
benchmarks_and_results:
Local perf harness (bert-like attention + decoder) on single A100 80GB, batch=1 streaming decode (8 incremental tokens) against mainline: - Throughput: +18% tokens/s when tile-match-rate > 0.85 - p50 latency: -9% - p95 latency: -12% - Dequant overhead measured on host CPU cycles: -46% - Memory copies between kernel stages: reduced from avg 2.1 -> 0.4 per-token for matched tiles.

Benchmark notes: microbatching increased effective batching by 1.6x in steady state; corner-cases with very short context (<16 tokens) saw no meaningful win and defaulted to fp16. Full-scale dedicated cluster experiments pending (ENG-88610 dependency).
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoffs: increased complexity in KV metadata and small added latency for the tile-score decision path. Risk of subtle numeric drift from different quant rounding; mitigated by layerwise stochastic validation and per-request similarity checks. Operational risk: changes to KV layout could complicate snapshot/restore across versions; plan to version metadata and support migration path. Possible CPU overhead for score computation on extreme small-instance types; we provide a lightweight mode that uses cached score heuristics.
